title: The importance of MRI for rectal cancer evaluation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《The importance of MRI for rectal cancer evaluation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has gained increasing importance in the management of rectal cancer over the last two decades.

evidence.text: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has gained increasing importance in the management of rectal cancer over the last two decades.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《The importance of MRI for rectal cancer evaluation》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】The role of MRI in patients with rectal cancer has expanded beyond the tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) system in both staging and restaging scenarios and has contributed to identifying "high" and "low" risk features that can be used to tailor and personalize patient treatment; for instance, selecting the patients for neoadjuvant chemoradiation (NCRT) before the total mesorectal excision (TME) surgery based on risk of recurrence.

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】As approaches using organ preservation emerge, including transanal local excision and "watch-and-wait", MRI may help in the patient selection for those treatments, follow up, and detection of tumor regrowth.

evidence.text: The role of MRI in patients with rectal cancer has expanded beyond the tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) system in both staging and restaging scenarios and has contributed to identifying "high" and "low" risk features that can be used to tailor and personalize patient treatment; for instance, selecting the patients for neoadjuvant chemoradiation (NCRT) before the total mesorectal excision (TME) surgery based on risk of recurrence.

As approaches using organ preservation emerge, including transanal local excision and "watch-and-wait", MRI may help in the patient selection for those treatments, follow up, and detection of tumor regrowth.
